sources.entry: altair - Declarative statistical visualization library for Python.

summary.one_liner: Vega-Altair is a declarative statistical visualization library for Python that builds charts on top of the Vega-Lite JSON specification.
summary.what_it_does: Provides a simple, consistent Python API for creating statistical charts with minimal code. Charts are built by chaining declarative calls (mark, encode, transforms) rather than writing imperative drawing code. The API is auto-generated from the Vega-Lite spec, so visualizations are type-checked and conform to that specification. It supports interactive features such as selections that link one chart to another, for example a brushed scatter plot filtering a bar chart. Charts can be displayed in JupyterLab, Jupyter Notebook, Visual Studio Code, GitHub and nbviewer, exported to PNG/SVG, standalone HTML or the Online Vega-Lite Editor, and serialized as JSON. The README includes a cars dataset example via altair.datasets.
use_cases: exploratory data analysis in Jupyter notebooks
interactive scatter plots with linked histograms
creating statistical charts from pandas DataFrames
exporting charts as PNG, SVG or HTML
notable: Declarative grammar that includes interaction (selections) as well as visual encoding
Python API auto-generated from the Vega-Lite specification with type checking
Multiple output options: notebook rendering, PNG/SVG, standalone HTML, JSON
Linked interactive views, such as a brush selection filtering a second chart
caveats: The README states the project is not affiliated with Altair Engineering, Inc., so it is unrelated to the similarly named company's products
Installation details beyond pip and conda are deferred to the external documentation
keywords: make charts from data in python
